subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should this PR's `gateway.peers` session-tool routing be accepted as the core cross-gateway session contract, or should implementation wait for the broader federation/identity design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733?
rationale: The choice changes Gateway trust boundaries, operator credentials, session visibility, message delivery, and transcript ownership, which automation cannot safely infer from code alone.

options.title: Design the contract first
options.body: Keep the PR open but block merge until maintainers define peer identity, token/scope rules, idempotency/replay behavior, and session-history ownership; this is the recommended path.

options.title: Narrow and repair this PR
options.body: Accept `gateway.peers` as the product shape, then require conflict resolution, the blocking runtime fixes, upgrade/security review, and real two-gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Close in favor of federation FRD
options.body: Pause this branch if maintainers decide the feature must land through a broader bridge protocol instead of session-tool URL parameters.

recommendation.title: Design the contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but block merge until maintainers define peer identity, token/scope rules, idempotency/replay behavior, and session-history ownership; this is the recommended path.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history is around gateway URL override/auth behavior and session-tool surfaces, which are the central security and product decision points.
